title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. pi_{0,3} is the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, free on two generators. Through the Legendre lambda-line it is identified with the level-2 modular curve Y(2), so pi_{0,3} is Gamma(2)/{±1}. On the previous page Grothendieck wrote down homomorphisms phi_infinity from pi^_{0,3} to SL(2,Z^)' and phi_{2m} from pi^_{0,3} to SL(2,Z/2m)'. These are the congruence quotients of the level-2 modular group; the prime ' plausibly means taking the quotient by ±1. Their images are the kernels of reduction mod 2, which gives the exact sequences (17) and (18). Their kernels are pi(infinity), the congruence kernel, and pi(2m).

Why squares appear. An outer automorphism of SL(2,Z/N)' coming from conjugation by an element of GL_2 depends only on its determinant d, through conjugation by diag(1,d). When d = a^2, diag(1,a^2) equals a times diag(a^{-1},a), so the conjugation is inner. Hence the units modulo squares, Z^*/Z^*2 (and (Z/2mZ)^*_2, units mod squares), act by outer automorphisms on pi^_{0,3}/pi(infinity) and on pi^_{0,3}/pi(2m).

This page. Compose the cyclotomic character chi : Gamma_Q -> Z^* with the projection to Z^*/Z^*2; this is (19). It gives an outer action of Gamma_Q on the congruence quotient pi^_{0,3}/pi(infinity). The 'condition des congruences' says that this action is compatible with the arithmetic outer action of Gamma_Q on pi^_{0,3} itself. On finite quotients the condition reads:
- pi(2m) is stable under the outer Galois action;
- the induced outer action on pi^_{0,3}/pi(2m) (a quotient isomorphic to Gamma(2)/±Gamma(2m)) is the one given by (20), Gamma_Q -> (Z/2mZ)^*_2, i.e. the cyclotomic character mod 2m, taken mod squares.

Arithmetically, this encodes the classical fact that the modular covers Y(2m) -> Y(2) are defined over Q, with Galois acting on the level structure through the determinant, i.e. the cyclotomic character.

Open points he records. He asks, as an 'exercice', whether this formulation is equivalent to the congruence conditions formulated in C^+_{1,1}, his group for the modular group in genus 1 with one puncture, or only a consequence of them. The next page asks whether these conditions really cut down a GT-type group (G-check_3) of outer automorphisms of pi^_{0,3}. He judges this probably out of reach, because the only known way to construct such automorphisms is arithmetic, via Gamma_Q.

Purpose. These are candidate defining conditions for a combinatorial/profinite substitute of Gamma_Q, the 'Teichmüller tower' programme. They would supplement the hexagon/pentagon-type relations with modular-congruence conditions.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The passage to units mod squares is correct for outer actions on SL(2)-type congruence quotients, because conjugation by diag(1,a^2) is inner.

The transcription's 'pi(2∞)' and '(Z/4Z)^*_2' are misreadings. The text is about pi(2m) and (Z/2mZ)^*_2, so the condition is a family indexed by all levels m, not a single 2-adic or level-4 condition.

ideas.what: Gamma_Q acts on the level-2 congruence tower of pi^_1(P^1-{0,1,inf}) = Gamma(2)^ by outer automorphisms factoring through the cyclotomic character mod squares (the field-of-definition/Galois action on modular curves Y(2m) -> Y(2)).
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on congruence quotients / modular tower, cyclotomic determinant
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Shimura); in the anabelian setting Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Not stated explicitly in Esquisse d'un programme as far as I know; the Longue Marche manuscripts discuss pi_{0,3} and SL2

ideas.what: Use the 'congruence condition' (compatibility of outer action with congruence quotients pi(2m)) as a defining constraint on GT-like groups of outer automorphisms of pi^_{0,3}, and question whether it is an effective restriction and whether it is equivalent to congruence conditions on C^+_{1,1}.
ideas.modern_name: Congruence/modular conditions on GT-hat; GT-hat action on SL2(Z)^ and congruence kernel
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ideas in Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Harbater–Schneps on GT-hat and genus 1/SL2(Z)^; Boggi on congruence subgroup properties

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes a 'congruence condition' as a constraint on outer automorphisms of pi^_{0,3}. Elements of a GT-type group should preserve every pi(2m), the kernel of pi^_{0,3} -> SL(2,Z/2m)', and act on the quotient through a character to (Z/2mZ)^*/squares, compatible with chi. He leaves open whether this is equivalent to congruence conditions on C^+_{1,1} and whether it genuinely restricts GT-hat. Whether every element of GT-hat satisfies such level-2m congruence compatibility is, to my knowledge, not explicitly settled in the literature under this formulation.
missed.quote: On devrait regarder si cette formulation est vraiment équivalente à celle des conditions de congruence dans C^+_{1,1} ... exercice !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give a concrete test of whether GT-hat is strictly larger than the image of Gamma_Q, by checking compatibility with congruence quotients. It links GT theory to the congruence subgroup problem for Gamma(2) and SL2(Z).

deep.surprise_reason: The arithmetic fact is classical. Formulating it as a candidate defining condition for GT-type groups, with the explicit equivalence question for genus (1,1), is a moderately interesting unpublished research thread. Related ideas exist in later GT/genus-1 literature, so it is not strikingly absent.
transcription_corrections: '(Z/4Z)^*_2' should read '(Z/2mZ)^*_2' in the map Z^*/Z^*2 -> (Z/2mZ)^*_2 and in (20): Gamma_Q -> (Z/2mZ)^*_2.
'Pour des groupes [?] continus [?]' is more likely 'Pour des quotients finis' or similar, referring to finite quotients at level 2m.
The first line reads roughly 'Gamma_Q sur les groupes (3.3 : toutes pi^_{0,3}), qui donne un composé'.
'conditions de congruence dans C^+_{1,1}': the hat over C^+_{1,1} is visible.
The last lines read: 'et non seulement une conséquence; exercice ! Par contre, la' (a deleted phrase precedes them).
